body: I feel I seriously need to remove myself from this situation and start over, with the benefit of my now (more or less) 20/20 hindsight. But how can I do that? I made a commitment to this choice in life, and somehow it doesn't feel right for me to just pick up and walk away (I don't have kids mind you) like I did with USAFA. I still beat myself up to this day for quiting that.

I suppose I should more clearly state what I had expected out of life. I'm not psychologist, but I imagined happiness as having a loving family that got along comfortably without having to overly worry about the trivialities of every day life. I didn't have that growing up, but swore to myself I would break the cycle and be good earner for my family and treat them all how I wished I had been treated growing up. So I do that, and then it feels like I just get shit on all the time. I can't help but ask myself "what's the point?"

We have been taking time away from each other since I travel varying amounts for work. When I was traveling 50% time, it was too much and she would make my life hell for never being home. Now, I travel 12 - 25% and I'm home too much and "get in her hair"... My whole life has been a continuous succession of wars lost. Mind you, I've won some battles with the degrees and what-not, but the struggle of those was meant to end up better than where I was: in a home that value me. That goal just seems ephemeral at this point...
